subject: Culture
title: Redefining Death
description: A quick, practical guide to Redefining Death.

hook.text: In 1968, Harvard redefined death as 'brain death.' Before that, a stopped heart was the only exit.

buildup.text: The definition was needed because ventilators kept bodies alive after brains stopped. Organ transplants needed clarity.

discovery.text: Japan didn't accept brain death until 1997. Families insisted the body was still alive if the heart still beat.

twist.text: Cryonics companies freeze bodies hoping future technology will revive them. Over 500 people are currently frozen.

climax.text: As technology blurs the line between alive and dead, culture must decide where personhood ends—and it keeps shifting.

punchline.text: We keep changing the definition of dead because we can't accept it.

quiz.question: When did Harvard redefine death as brain death?
